# MCP server catalog — independent re-verification (2026-09-26)

Second-pass verification of the 30-entry catalog. Every remote endpoint was probed
from this container (through the session's egress proxy) with three requests, each
with a 15 s timeout:

1. `POST <url>` — JSON-RPC `initialize` (protocolVersion 2025-06-18), no credentials
2. `GET <url>` with `Accept: text/event-stream`
3. `POST` initialize again with `Authorization: Bearer dummy-token-verify`, plus the
   vendor's own header with a dummy value where the catalog named one
   (`x-api-key`, `X-API-Key`, `X-Api-Key`, `Close-API-Key`, `x-api-token`,
   `Sentry-Bearer`, `Basic`).

Every stdio package was checked with `npm view <pkg> version` (or PyPI JSON for the
Python one), its README pulled from npm or raw.githubusercontent.com, and the tarball
unpacked and grepped for `process.env.*` so the env-var name comes from the code,
not from prose. Every `docs_url` was fetched and the load-bearing sentence grepped
out of the rendered text. Raw probe output is under `research/probe/out/*.txt`,
READMEs under `research/probe/readme/` and `research/probe/gh/`, unpacked packages
under `research/probe/pkg/`.

Note on the proxy: `github.com` HTML pages answer 403 to curl through this egress
proxy, but `raw.githubusercontent.com` answers 200, so every GitHub-hosted README was
read from the raw host; the 403 is the proxy, not a missing repo.

**Result: all 30 entries exist, on the transport the catalog states, and none of them
requires a token in the URL. Nothing is dropped. Six entries are corrected (marked
FIX), and a handful of notes are tightened (marked NOTE).**

## Corrections to the first catalog

| # | Entry | What was wrong | Verified fact |
|---|---|---|---|
| FIX 1 | Zapier | `endpoint` was `https://mcp.zapier.com/api/mcp/mcp`. That URL answers 401 *"Expected Bearer token for MCP authentication"*, but it appears nowhere in Zapier's docs. | The documented connection-token endpoint is **`https://mcp.zapier.com/api/v1/connect`** with `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_CONNECTION_TOKEN` (docs.zapier.com/mcp/overview/how-connections-work and /mcp/get-started/connect/other). Probed: POST 401 *"Missing authorization header or token query parameter"* with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=…/api/v1/connect`; GET 401; Bearer-dummy → *"Invalid OAuth token - please re-authenticate"*. The query-parameter form (`?t=…`) the same page offers is the §2.3 rejection. |
| FIX 2 | Neon (stdio note) | "The stdio `@neondatabase/mcp-server-neon` is deprecated and reads `NEON_AUTH_HEADER`." | `NEON_AUTH_HEADER` is a variable in the docs' **mcp-remote** recipe (`"env": {"NEON_AUTH_HEADER": "Bearer <YOUR_NEON_API_KEY>"}` passed as `--header Authorization:${NEON_AUTH_HEADER}`), not something the package reads. The package (0.6.5, npm-deprecated: *"Use the remote MCP server at mcp.neon.tech instead"*) reads **no key from `process.env`** at all; it takes the key as a **positional command-line argument** — `npx -y @neondatabase/mcp-server-neon start <YOUR_NEON_API_KEY>`, and its error text is *"Please provide a NEON_API_KEY as a command-line argument"*. That is ps-visible. Do not use the stdio package; the hosted server is the only sane path. |
| FIX 3 | Neon (probe note) | "Bearer-dummy 401 (parsed)". | Bearer-dummy returns the **identical** body to no-auth: `{"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"No authorization provided"}`. The server does not distinguish a malformed token from none, so nothing about header parsing can be inferred from outside. |
| FIX 4 | Sentry (stdio note) | Only the env var was named. | The package (0.42.0) accepts **both** `--access-token=<token>` on the command line (the README's primary examples, 34 mentions, ps-visible) and `SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN` (source: `if (env.SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN) fromEnv.accessToken = …`, help text: *"alternative to --access-token"*). Use the env var. `SENTRY_HOST` confirmed. |
| FIX 5 | Stripe (stdio note) | "stdio `@stripe/mcp` passes the key as `--api-key` on the command line (visible in ps)". | True, but incomplete: the package (0.3.3) also reads **`STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`** from the environment (`process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` ×7; README: *"Alternatively, you could set the STRIPE_SECRET_KEY in your environment variables"*). |
| FIX 6 | Context7 (stdio note) | "The stdio `--api-key` flag is visible in ps — prefer the hosted server." | Same shape: the package (4.1.1) also reads **`CONTEXT7_API_KEY`** (`process.env.CONTEXT7_API_KEY`; README: *"You can use the CONTEXT7_API_KEY environment variable instead of passing the --api-key flag"*). |
| NOTE 7 | Atlassian | "/v1/mcp and /v1/sse also 401". | True without credentials, but **`/v1/mcp` answers 200 to a dummy Bearer** (initialize succeeds, `atlassian-mcp-server`), i.e. v1 checks the token at call time; **v2 refuses at initialize** (401 for none, Bearer-dummy and Basic-dummy alike). Test connection against v2, never v1. Also: the docs URL now redirects to `support.atlassian.com/atlassian-ai-gateway/docs/configure-authentication-via-api-token/` — the product page was renamed "Atlassian AI Gateway"; the content still quotes both `Authorization: Basic <base64(email:api_token)>` and `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. |
| NOTE 8 | Pipedrive | "x-api-token-dummy → 200". | Stronger than stated: with a dummy `x-api-token`, `initialize` → 200, `notifications/initialized` → 202, and **`tools/list` → 200 with the full tool list** (`getActivities`, …). The header is definitely read (a dummy `Bearer` fails with *"Invalid token format."*), but the value is not validated until a tool call. Test connection proves nothing about the token. |
| NOTE 9 | Exa | "tools/list without auth returned web_search_exa". | Keyless `tools/list` now returns **two** tools: `web_search_exa` and `web_fetch_exa`. |
| NOTE 10 | Hugging Face | "env DEFAULT_HF_TOKEN then HF_TOKEN". | `process.env.DEFAULT_HF_TOKEN` is read (×9) in the bundled source; `HF_TOKEN` appears only in README prose (*"If running with stdio transport, HF_TOKEN is used if DEFAULT_HF_TOKEN is not set"*) and UI strings — no literal `process.env.HF_TOKEN` read was found in the bundle. Set `DEFAULT_HF_TOKEN`. Package is `@llmindset/hf-mcp-server` **0.4.23** on npm (the catalog gave no version). |
| NOTE 11 | Firecrawl | "REJECT the `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/{API_KEY}/v2/sse` URL form". | That form is no longer in the README or the docs page; the rule stands as "reject if seen" but it is historical. Two other facts worth having: the keyless hosted `/v2/mcp` exposes only **3** tools (`firecrawl_scrape`, `firecrawl_search`, `firecrawl_parse`), and `/v2/mcp-search` is OAuth-only (401 *"OAuth access token required"* even with an API key as Bearer). `/v2/mcp-oauth` with a Bearer dummy answers `invalid_api_key … auth_mode: api_key`, so that path also accepts an API key as Bearer. |
| NOTE 12 | Snyk | Cheat-sheet args quoted as `snyk@latest`. | The vendor's own cheat sheet literally says `"snyk@lastest"` (typo); use `snyk@latest`. `npx -y snyk@1.1307.4 mcp --help` confirms `-t, --transport string sets transport to <stdio> (default "stdio")`. The docs URL now redirects to `docs.snyk.io/agent-security`. The "≥ v1.1298.0" requirement and the *"must use SNYK_TOKEN for the Secret Name"* quote were not found on the pages fetched — not contradicted, not re-verified. |
| NOTE 13 | Cal.com | "62 tools". | 62 is the **hosted** server's count (docs page). The stdio package (0.0.6) enables **9** core tools by default and needs `--all-tools` for the rest; its README opens with an "active development, subject to rapid changes" warning. |
| NOTE 14 | GitHub | `X-MCP-Toolsets` / `X-MCP-Readonly`. | Confirmed, but from `docs/remote-server.md`, not the README (the README no longer lists them). Full set: `X-MCP-Toolsets`, `X-MCP-Tools`, `X-MCP-Readonly`, `X-MCP-Insiders`, `X-MCP-Lockdown`; per-toolset URLs `…/mcp/x/<toolset>[/readonly]`. |
| NOTE 15 | Cloudflare / Zapier docs URLs | — | Both redirect: Cloudflare to `developers.cloudflare.com/agents/model-context-protocol/cloudflare/servers-for-cloudflare/`, Zapier's `/mcp/get-started/connect` to `/mcp/get-started/quickstart`. Exa's redirects to `exa.ai/docs/get-started/exa-mcp`. Content unchanged; update the links. |

## Verified table

Columns: **POST** = status of unauthenticated `initialize`; **GET** = status of the GET;
**Bearer-dummy** = what a garbage Bearer token gets at `initialize`. "checked at call
time" means a bad token is accepted at `initialize` and only refused on `tools/call`,
so Test connection cannot prove the credential.

## Class legend (unchanged from the first catalog)

- **A** — `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`; the worker's injected header works as-is: Exa, Firecrawl, Tavily, Jina, Context7, Hugging Face, Linear, Intercom, Atlassian (service-account key), Zapier, GitHub, Cloudflare, Neon, Stripe.
- **B** — a named header or scheme the worker cannot set today: Hunter (`X-API-Key`), Apollo (`X-Api-Key`), Close (`Close-API-Key` + `Close-Scope`), Pipedrive (`x-api-token`), Sentry (`Sentry-Bearer` scheme).
- **C** — OAuth only, needs a connect flow + refresh in the product: HubSpot, Attio, Slack, Notion (hosted), Asana, Cal.com (hosted), Calendly (DCR).
- **D** — stdio, env var other than `MCP_SECRET`: Brave (`BRAVE_API_KEY`), Snyk (`SNYK_TOKEN`), Semgrep (`SEMGREP_APP_TOKEN`), Notion stdio (`NOTION_TOKEN`), Cal.com stdio (`CAL_API_KEY`).
- No auth: DeepWiki, `docs.mcp.cloudflare.com`.

## Where Test connection cannot prove the credential

`initialize` succeeds with a garbage token on: Exa, Firecrawl (`/v2/mcp`), Jina, Context7, DeepWiki, Intercom, Pipedrive (`x-api-token`; even `tools/list` succeeds), Atlassian **v1**, Sentry (`Sentry-Bearer`), Semgrep hosted. For those, a connector test needs a `tools/call`.

## Explicitly not verified here

- Any real credential — every probe used a dummy. "Parsed" means the server's error text changed with the header; it never means the header works.
- Hourly token expiry (Asana), rate-limit figures (Attio, Slack), Rovo credit consumption (Atlassian), the Snyk CLI minimum version.
- Whether Zapier's undocumented `/api/mcp/mcp` accepts a connection token as Bearer; use the documented `/api/v1/connect`.
